name: The Mariner
blurb: A rented room above the waterfront. Thin walls. One stairway. Yours, for now.

name: Saint Agnes
blurb: Coffee by daylight, whispered arrangements after dark. Your contact keeps the corner booth.

name: Pier 14
blurb: Cargo arrives every morning. Honest work and less honest favors both pay cash.

name: Bluebird Laundry
blurb: A neighborhood business seeking protection. A small beginning, if you can honor the arrangement.

name: The Monarch
blurb: Bellandi men watch the doors. This casino belongs to a family that does not tolerate outsiders making demands.

name: Mercer Exchange
blurb: People sell information here. Its value depends on whom you ask, and who sees you asking.

name: Ashbury Court
blurb: A private entrance, a respectable address, and a landlord willing to mind his own business.

name: Russo Motor Works
blurb: A working garage at the edge of Russo territory. An investment that requires political tact.

name: The Blue Hour
blurb: A shuttered gambling house. Restore its reputation and the tables could support an entire crew.

name: Cypress House
blurb: High walls above the city. A statement of success, and a very conspicuous address.

name: Ward Street Station
blurb: Grey stone and a desk sergeant who has seen everybody. Nothing here is for sale and everything here is for trade.

name: The Bellwether Herald
blurb: Three floors of typewriters and one man on the top one who decides what the city read this morning.

name: Vittoria's
blurb: A family restaurant with a back room nobody books. The kitchen pays for itself; the room is worth more.

name: The Green Baize
blurb: Six tables and a payphone that rings at the same hour every night. Somebody is running a book on it already.

name: Fassano Meats
blurb: A cold room, a van, and a licence to move refrigerated goods across the river at any hour.

name: Kerrigan Haulage
blurb: Four trucks and a yard. Whatever leaves this city on wheels leaves on somebody's timetable.

name: The Golden Lily
blurb: A second house across the river, quieter than the Blue Hour and harder to get into. The same game, a different room.

name: Ordway Steam Laundry
blurb: A bigger laundry than the Bluebird, on a street that never asks what is in the vans.

name: The Paper Moon
blurb: A revue bar with a stage, a late licence and a room upstairs. What is worth having here is who comes through the door.

name: Vance Cab Company
blurb: Eleven cars and a dispatcher who knows where everybody went. A cab is a business and it is also a pair of eyes.

name: Ferris Motor Sales
blurb: A lot with a dozen cars on it and a man who knows what everybody in this city drives. Every car in Bellwether came off somebody's forecourt.

name: Archway Motor Repairs
blurb: A second yard, under the viaduct, where nobody asks what came in on the back of the truck.

name: Devlin Salvage
blurb: Six acres of what the city used to drive, stacked four high. Everything ends up here, and somebody pays for the privilege of leaving it.

name: Kessler's Filling Station
blurb: Two pumps, a tin roof and a rack of everything a person remembers wanting once they have stopped: oil, cigarettes, a map of a city they already live in.

name: The Viaduct Pumps
blurb: Under the arches on the way out of town, open when nowhere else is, which is worth more than the petrol.

name: Ackerman & Son
blurb: Three brass balls over the door and a window of other people's things. Open late, and nobody in it asks where anything came from.
